items.descriptionOriginal: Η προστασία της καρδιάς συνδέεται με το σύνολο των καθημερινών διατροφικών επιλογών. Τρόφιμα φυτικής προέλευσης με ελάχιστη επεξεργασία, κατάλληλες πηγές λιπαρών και πρωτεΐνης και περιορισμός προϊόντων με πρόσθετη ζάχαρη και πολύ αλάτι βρίσκονται στο επίκεντρο νέας επιστημονικής δήλωσης του Αμερικανικού Κολεγίου Καρδιολογίας (ACC). Η κεντρική γραμμή είναι ότι η συνολική ποιότητα της διατροφής και η συνέπεια στις υγιεινές επιλογές έχουν μεγαλύτερη σημασία από την προσήλωση σε ένα μεμονωμένο τρόφιμο ή θρεπτικό συστατικό. Η δήλωση, η οποία δημοσιεύθηκε στο Journal of the American College of Cardiology (JACC) , συνθέτει υπάρχοντα επιστημονικά δεδομένα για τη διατροφή στην πρόληψη και τη διαχείριση των καρδιαγγειακών νοσημάτων. Βασίζεται σε κλινικές δοκιμές, μελέτες παρακολούθησης πληθυσμών και έρευνες για τους βιολογικούς μηχανισμούς που συνδέουν τη διατροφή με την υγεία. Από τα θρεπτικά συστατικά στο καθημερινό διαιτολόγιο Όπως εξηγεί ο Δρ. Frank B. Hu, πρόεδρος της επιτροπής συγγραφής, η επιστημονική προσέγγιση έχει εξελιχθεί: η έμφαση μετατοπίζεται από την εξέταση μεμονωμένων θρεπτικών συστατικών προς τα τρόφιμα και τα διατροφικά πρότυπα, που αποτυπώνουν πληρέστερα τη σύνθετη σχέση διατροφής και καρδιομεταβολικής υγείας. Η προσέγγιση αυτή αφορά τόσο την πρόληψη της εμφάνισης καρδιαγγειακής νόσου όσο και τη φροντίδα ανθρώπων που έχουν ήδη διαγνωστεί. Η διατροφική παρέμβαση εντάσσεται στη συνολική αντιμετώπιση, μαζί με τις υπόλοιπες θεραπευτικές παρεμβάσεις που χρειάζεται κάθε ασθενής. Οι αλλαγές που υποστηρίζουν τα δεδομένα Οι συντάκτες δίνουν έμφαση: Στην αντικατάσταση των κορεσμένων λιπαρών με ακόρεστα , αναδεικνύοντας τη σημασία της ποιότητας των λιπαρών στη διατροφή. Στην αυξημένη πρόσληψη φυτικών ινών και στην κατανάλωση προϊόντων ολικής άλεσης. Στη μείωση του νατρίου και στον περιορισμό υπερεπεξεργασμένων τροφίμων χαμηλής διατροφικής αξίας, ιδιαίτερα ζαχαρούχων ποτών και επεξεργασμένου κρέατος. Στη σταθερή υιοθέτηση υγιεινών διατροφικών προτύπων που μπορούν να διατηρηθούν μακροπρόθεσμα. Η μεσογειακή διατροφή , η DASH -διατροφική προσέγγιση για την αντιμετώπιση της υπέρτασης- και υγιεινά χορτοφαγικά ή άλλα πρότυπα πλούσια σε φυτικά τρόφιμα παρουσιάζουν ευνοϊκές επιδράσεις στην αρτηριακή πίεση, στα λιπίδια, στη ρύθμιση του σακχάρου και στο σωματικό βάρος. Παράλληλα, συνδέονται με χαμηλότερα ποσοστά καρδιαγγειακών νοσημάτων και θνησιμότητας. Τι συστήνεται για τα ποτά Σύμφωνα με την επίσημη ανακοίνωση του ACC, προτεραιότητα πρέπει να έχουν το νερό και τα μη ζαχαρούχα ποτά , με περιορισμό όσων περιέχουν πρόσθετη ζάχαρη. Για το αλκοόλ , η σύσταση είναι να περιορίζεται ή να αποφεύγεται η κατανάλωσή του. Η σύνδεση καρδιάς, νεφρών και μεταβολισμού Η δήλωση εξετάζει τη διατροφή και στο πλαίσιο του καρδιαγγειακού-νεφρικού-μεταβολικού συνδρόμου (CKM) , το οποίο περιγράφει την αλληλεπίδραση διαταραχών του μεταβολισμού, της νεφρικής λειτουργίας και του καρδιαγγειακού συστήματος. Η παχυσαρκία, ο διαβήτης, η χρόνια νεφρική νόσος και τα καρδιαγγειακά νοσήματα εξετάζονται ως αλληλένδετα προβλήματα. Η σημασία της διατροφικής φροντίδας, επομένως, εκτείνεται πέρα από τη διαχείριση του βάρους. Οι συγγραφείς αναφέρονται και στους αγωνιστές του υποδοχέα GLP-1 . Παρότι αυτές οι θεραπείες μπορούν να προσφέρουν σημαντική απώλεια βάρους και καρδιαγγειακά οφέλη, η ποιοτική διατροφή με επάρκεια θρεπτικών συστατικών παραμένει σημαντική κατά τη λήψη τους. Η πρόσβαση στα τρόφιμα αποτελεί μέρος της πρόληψης Η εφαρμογή των συστάσεων εξαρτάται και από τις συνθήκες ζωής . Το κόστος, η διαθεσιμότητα και η πρόσβαση σε θρεπτικά τρόφιμα επηρεάζουν την ποιότητα της διατροφής. Γι’ αυτό, η δήλωση υπογραμμίζει τη σημασία της επισιτιστικής ασφάλειας: τα κατάλληλα τρόφιμα χρειάζεται να είναι διαθέσιμα, οικονομικά προσιτά και προσβάσιμα, ενώ οι άνθρωποι πρέπει να έχουν τη δυνατότητα να τα αξιοποιούν στην καθημερινότητά τους. Όπως συνοψίζει ο Δρ. Hu, το ζητούμενο είναι ένα σταθερό πρότυπο ποιοτικών διατροφικών επιλογών που υποστηρίζει την καρδιομεταβολική υγεία και μπορεί να διατηρηθεί στον χρόνο. Διαβάστε επίσης Πώς θα προστατέψουμε την καρδιά με 5 απλά βήματα, σύμφωνα με καρδιολόγο Όχι και τόσο αθώα τα αναψυκτικά χωρίς ζάχαρη – Πώς αυξάνουν τον κίνδυνο για την καρδιά Τι θα συμβεί αν πίνουμε ένα σφηνάκι ελαιόλαδο κάθε μέρα – Απαντά η Λίνσεϊ που το δοκίμασε για 2 εβδομάδες

Η ιδέα είναι απλή: Αν διευκολυνθεί η έξοδος των άχρηστων – επιβαρυντικών ουσιών, θα μπορούσε να περιοριστεί και η βλάβη που προκαλούν… Μια νέα χειρουργική τεχνική επιχειρεί να μετατρέψει αυτή την υπόθεση σε θεραπευτική παρέμβαση, γεννώντας υψηλές προσδοκίες αλλά και σοβαρές επιφυλάξεις. Η τεχνική περιγράφηκε για πρώτη φορά σε κινεζικό επιστημονικό περιοδικό το 2022 και έκτοτε έχει εφαρμοστεί χιλιάδες φορές σε νοσοκομεία της Κίνας. Η έρευνα, ωστόσο, δεν έχει ακολουθήσει τον ίδιο ρυθμό: Μέχρι σήμερα οι δημοσιευμένες μελέτες ήταν μικρές, πραγματοποιήθηκαν σε μεμονωμένα κέντρα και δεν αποτελούσαν κλινικές δοκιμές. Τώρα, όπως αναφέρει το Science Focus, του BBC, ελεγχόμενες δοκιμές της τεχνικής αρχίζουν εκτός από την Κίνα και στις ΗΠΑ και στη Νότια Κορέα. Νέες αποκαλυπτικές συνομιλίες που περιλαμβάνονται στο υλικό της υπόθεσης φωτίζουν τον τρόπο με τον οποίο φέρονται να διαχειρίζονταν τα χρήματα…
items.descriptionOriginal: Οργή προκαλούν οι αποκαλύψεις για τη δράση της εγκληματικής οργάνωσης που φέρεται να δρούσε υπό τον μανδύα φιλανθρωπικής ΜΚΟ στη Βόρεια Ελλάδα, εκμεταλλευόμενη τον ανθρώπινο πόνο και την αγωνία οικογενειών με παιδιά που αντιμετώπιζαν σοβαρές ασθένειες. Νέες αποκαλυπτικές συνομιλίες που περιλαμβάνονται στο υλικό της υπόθεσης φωτίζουν τον τρόπο με τον οποίο φέρονται να διαχειρίζονταν τα χρήματα της ΜΚΟ τα βασικά μέλη της οργάνωσης. Στους διαλόγους, ένα ζευγάρι εμφανίζεται να συζητά για χιλιάδες ευρώ που είχαν δαπανηθεί μέσα σε λίγες ημέρες, χωρίς, όπως προκύπτει από τη συνομιλία, να έχουν σαφή εικόνα για το πού κατέληγαν όλα τα χρήματα. Σε μία από τις συνομιλίες, η γυναίκα εμφανίζεται σοκαρισμένη από το ύψος των δαπανών, λέγοντας χαρακτηριστικά: « Έχω πάθει σοκ. Έχουμε φάει τόσες χιλιάδες μέσα σε λίγες μέρες. Ας ηρεμήσουμε λίγο ». Ο άνδρας επιχειρεί να διευκρινίσει τις συναλλαγές, αναφέροντας ότι είχε μεταφέρει 6.000 ευρώ μέσω Revolut , ενώ η γυναίκα αναρωτιέται τι ακριβώς έχει ξοδέψει η ίδια, κάνοντας αναφορά σε ποσά 6.000 και 7.000 ευρώ, αλλά και σε αγορές, όπως ένα φόρεμα αξίας 200 ευρώ και αεροπορικά εισιτήρια. Οι διάλογοι αποτυπώνουν την οικονομική άνεση με την οποία φέρονται να κινούνταν οι δύο κατηγορούμενοι, την ώρα που οι δωρεές είχαν συγκεντρωθεί στο όνομα παιδιών με σοβαρά προβλήματα υγείας. Σε δεύτερη συνομιλία, γίνεται αναφορά στην προσέγγιση γνωστού τραγουδιστή , από τον οποίο επιχειρούσαν να εξασφαλίσουν οικονομική ενίσχυση. Το ζευγάρι συζητά για την τηλεφωνική επικοινωνία και για ένα ποσό που φέρεται να προτάθηκε αρχικά, με σκοπό την κάλυψη συγκεκριμένης ανάγκης οικογένειας. Από τη συνομιλία προκύπτει ότι η επικοινωνία με επώνυμα πρόσωπα αποτελούσε μέρος της πρακτικής προσέλκυσης δωρεών, ενώ εξεταζόταν και το ενδεχόμενο να ζητηθεί πρόσθετη οικονομική συνεισφορά. Ιδιαίτερο ενδιαφέρον παρουσιάζει και τρίτη συνομιλία, στην οποία η γυναίκα επικοινωνεί με κέντρο αισθητικής , ζητώντας πληροφορίες για ιατρικές παρεμβάσεις που αφορούν την αντιμετώπιση ασυμμετρίας. Μάλιστα, δηλώνει χαρακτηριστικά ότι δεν την απασχολεί το κόστος και ότι επιθυμεί να συζητήσει απευθείας με τον γιατρό. Υπενθυμίζεται ότι για την υπόθεση συνελήφθησαν έξι άτομα , μεταξύ των οποίων ο 37χρονος ιδρυτής της ΜΚΟ «Παιδική Χαρά». Σύμφωνα με την εκπρόσωπο Τύπου της ΕΛ.ΑΣ., Κωνσταντία Δημογλίδου , το συνολικό ποσό που φέρεται να συγκεντρώθηκε από τις ερανικές δράσεις αγγίζει τα 4 εκατομμύρια ευρώ, ενώ μόλις περίπου 1 εκατομμύριο ευρώ εκτιμάται ότι έφτασε στις οικογένειες που είχαν ανάγκη. Τα υπόλοιπα χρήματα φέρονται να αποτέλεσαν παράνομο οικονομικό όφελος για τα μέλη της οργάνωσης. Η μεθοδολογία και τα θύματα Η οργάνωση φέρεται να ξεκίνησε τη δράση της τουλάχιστον από τον Οκτώβριο του 2018 . Ως βασικά πρόσωπα εμφανίζονται ένας 37χρονος παράγοντας του τοπικού ποδοσφαίρου και η 35χρονη σύζυγός του, οι οποίοι φέρονται να είχαν αναλάβει τον συντονισμό της δραστηριότητας. Η μέθοδος που ακολουθούσαν βασιζόταν στη δημοσιοποίηση φωτογραφιών παιδιών με σοβαρά προβλήματα υγείας στα μέσα κοινωνικής δικτύωσης και στην προβολή των οικονομικών αναγκών των οικογενειών τους. Οι δωρητές καλούνταν να συνεισφέρουν για θεραπείες, νοσηλείες και έξοδα διαβίωσης, ακόμη και σε περιπτώσεις όπου, σύμφωνα με την αστυνομική έρευνα, οι συγκεκριμένες δαπάνες είχαν ήδη καλυφθεί από ασφαλιστικά ταμεία ή εμφανίζονταν τεχνητά διογκωμένες. Σύμφωνα με τα στοιχεία της έρευνας, καταγράφηκαν συνολικά 92 ερανικές δράσεις για 74 ωφελούμενα πρόσωπα , από τα οποία τα 55 έχουν ταυτοποιηθεί. Οι έρανοι πραγματοποιούνταν χωρίς τις προβλεπόμενες νόμιμες άδειες. Ιδιαίτερα αποκαλυπτικές είναι οι περιπτώσεις οικογενειών που περίμεναν να λάβουν την οικονομική βοήθεια που είχε συγκεντρωθεί στο όνομα των παιδιών τους. Για παιδί που έπασχε από λευχαιμία και κατέληξε το 2021 συγκεντρώθηκαν περισσότερα από 136.000 ευρώ για έξοδα διαβίωσης και κηδείας. Στην οικογένεια, ωστόσο, φέρεται να αποδόθηκαν μόλις 7.000 ευρώ . Ανάλογη είναι η εικόνα και στην περίπτωση 14χρονου παιδιού που πέθανε το 2026 . Για την ενίσχυση της οικογένειάς του συγκεντρώθηκαν 340.421 ευρώ, ωστόσο στους οικείους του φέρεται να έφτασαν μόλις 55.800 ευρώ. Σε άλλη περίπτωση, οικογένεια 15χρονου δεν έλαβε κανένα ποσό από τον έρανο, ύψους 73.000 ευρώ , με την οργάνωση να επικαλείται, σύμφωνα με την έρευνα, τραπεζικά κωλύματα. Η εκμετάλλευση επώνυμων δωρητών Σημαντικό ρόλο στην ανάπτυξη της δραστηριότητας της ΜΚΟ φέρεται να έπαιξε η εμπιστοσύνη που κέρδισε από γνωστούς καλλιτέχνες, αθλητές και επιχειρηματίες . Οι δωρεές επωνύμων δημοσιοποιούνταν στα μέσα κοινωνικής δικτύωσης και χρησιμοποιούνταν ως διαπιστευτήριο αξιοπιστίας, προσελκύοντας ακόμη περισσότερους πολίτες. Σε αναρτήσεις της, η «Παιδική Χαρά» παρουσίαζε τις οικονομικές ανάγκες συγκεκριμένων παιδιών ως επείγουσες, ανακοινώνοντας παράλληλα τις συνεισφορές γνωστών προσώπων. Με αυτόν τον τρόπο δημιουργούνταν η εικόνα ενός οργανωμένου φιλανθρωπικού φορέα, με σημαντική κοινωνική αποδοχή και τη στήριξη επώνυμων δωρητών. Μεταξύ όσων συνέβαλαν οικονομικά ήταν και ο αντιδήμαρχος Κορδελιού – Ευόσμου , Παναγιώτης Καμπαρούδης. « Ένας από αυτούς ήμουν και εγώ, που για άλλο παιδί έχω καταθέσει χρήματα σε λογαριασμούς που κατά καιρούς δημοσίευσε η οργάνωση. Απογοήτευση και μόνο », ανέφερε χαρακτηριστικά. Το ξέπλυμα χρήματος και ο στοιχηματισμός Συνολικά, στους τραπεζικούς λογαριασμούς της ΜΚΟ εντοπίστηκαν καταθέσεις που ξεπερνούν τα 5,8 εκατομμύρια ευρώ . Οι αρχές εξετάζουν τη διαδρομή των χρημάτων και τον τρόπο με τον οποίο φέρονται να διοχετεύονταν σε προσωπικούς λογαριασμούς και άλλες δραστηριότητες. Ενδεικτική της οικονομικής διαχείρισης που περιγράφεται στη δικογραφία είναι συνομιλία μεταξύ δύο βασικών κατηγορουμένων , στην οποία γίνεται αναφορά στον όγκο των συναλλαγών και στα ποσά που είχαν δαπανηθεί μέσα σε λίγες ημέρες. Το πιο εντυπωσιακό εύρημα αφορά τη σύνδεση της υπόθεσης με τον στοιχηματισμό . Σύμφωνα με την αστυνομική έρευνα, ο 37χρονος φέρεται να πίστωσε σε στοιχηματικούς λογαριασμούς περισσότερα από 2,6 εκατομμύρια ευρώ, επιχειρώντας να εμφανίσει χρήματα από τις δωρεές ως νόμιμα κέρδη από τυχερά παιχνίδια. Από την πλευρά του, ο συνήγορος του κατηγορουμένου, Κώστας Παπαδόπουλος , αρνείται οποιαδήποτε εμπλοκή του εντολέα του σε στημένους ποδοσφαιρικούς αγώνες. « Δεν έχει καμία απολύτως σχέση με στημένα παιχνίδια. Ενοχοποιείται διότι σε κάποιες τηλεφωνικές συνομιλίες τρίτων γινόταν αναφορά στο όνομά του ως διαιτητή τον οποίο δήθεν ήλεγχαν », δήλωσε. Ως σημείο συνάντησης και συντονισμού της οργάνωσης φέρεται να χρησιμοποιούνταν καφετέρια στην Καλαμαριά , την οποία είχε ανοίξει ο 37χρονος. Εκεί πραγματοποιούνταν συναντήσεις και λαμβάνονταν αποφάσεις για τη διαχείριση και την κατανομή των χρημάτων που συγκεντρώνονταν από τις δωρεές. Παράλληλα, ο 32χρονος κουνιάδος του φερόμενου ως αρχηγού φέρεται να είχε αναλάβει τη λογιστική διαχείριση εικονικών εταιρειών που συνδέονται με τη δραστηριότητα της οργάνωσης. Τα στημένα παιχνίδια της Πιερίας Η δράση της οργάνωσης, σύμφωνα με τη δικογραφία, δεν περιοριζόταν στην οικονομική εκμετάλλευση των εράνων, αλλά επεκτεινόταν και στον χώρο του ερασιτεχνικού ποδοσφαίρου . Ο 37χρονος φέρεται να χρηματοδότησε με περίπου 250.000 ευρώ δύο ερασιτεχνικές ομάδες στην Πιερία . Στόχος, σύμφωνα με τις αρχές, ήταν η εξαγορά διαιτητών με αμοιβές που έφταναν έως και τα 1.000 ευρώ ανά αγώνα, προκειμένου να εξασφαλιστεί η άνοδος συγκεκριμένης ομάδας στη Γ’ Εθνική. Σύμφωνα με την έρευνα, το κύκλωμα φέρεται να χρησιμοποιούσε τον τοπικό αρχιδιαιτητή για να επηρεάζει την έκβαση αγώνων και να αποκομίζει κέρδη μέσω παράνομου στοιχηματισμού. Στη δικογραφία περιλαμβάνονται, επίσης, στοιχεία για live στοιχηματισμό με εσωτερική πληροφόρηση σε αγώνα της Super League Κ19 , καθώς και 62 προσωπικά στοιχήματα του 37χρονου, ο οποίος φέρεται να πόνταρε συστηματικά στην ήττα συγκεκριμένης ομάδας. Από το πρόσωπο του εθελοντή στην αστυνομική έρευνα Ο 37χρονος ιδρυτής της «Παιδικής Χαράς» είχε παρουσιάσει δημόσια τη δράση του σωματείου ήδη από το 2013 , μέσα από τη συχνότητα της ΕΡΤ3, συστηνόμενος ως άνθρωπος που ήθελε να στηρίξει οικογένειες και παιδιά με σοβαρά προβλήματα υγείας. Σε τηλεοπτική του εμφάνιση, ως πρόεδρος του σωματείου, ο Κωνσταντίνος Φιρινίδης είχε αναφερθεί στην προσπάθεια δημιουργίας μιας ομάδας εθελοντών που θα προσέφερε ουσιαστική βοήθεια σε οικογένειες που αντιμετώπιζαν δύσκολες καταστάσεις. Όπως είχε εξηγήσει, η πρωτοβουλία ξεκίνησε από μια προσωπική εμπειρία , καθώς ένα ανιψάκι του αντιμετώπιζε σοβαρό πρόβλημα υγείας. Μαζί με άλλα 20 μέλη, όπως είχε αναφέρει, αποφάσισαν να δημιουργήσουν τη δική τους ομάδα, οργανώνοντας δράσεις και εκδηλώσεις για την ενίσχυση οικογενειών που είχαν ανάγκη. Το 2018 το σωματείο απέκτησε επίσημα νομική υπόσταση ως ΜΚΟ με την επωνυμία «Παιδική Χαρά» . Μέσα από τα μέσα κοινωνικής δικτύωσης παρουσίαζε συστηματικά τις δράσεις του, αναρτώντας φωτογραφίες παιδιών που νοσούσαν και εκκλήσεις για οικονομική ενίσχυση. Σε χαρακτηριστική ανάρτηση αναφερόταν: « Ένα παιδί παλεύει για τη ζωή του και οι γονείς του παλεύουν να μπορέσουν απλώς να είναι δίπλα του. Ας μην τους αφήσουμε μόνους ». Σε άλλη δημοσίευση, το σωματείο ανακοίνωνε ότι μέσα σε μόλις τρεις ημέρες είχε καλυφθεί η οικονομική ανάγκη ενός παιδιού, έπειτα από δωρεές πολιτών και γνωστού διεθνούς ποδοσφαιριστή, ο οποίος είχε συνεισφέρει 12.500 ευρώ. Η δημόσια εικόνα της φιλανθρωπικής δραστηριότητας, οι επώνυμες δωρεές και οι συνεχείς εκκλήσεις για βοήθεια φέρονται να συνέβαλαν στην προσέλκυση ολοένα και περισσότερων δωρητών. Πίσω από αυτή την εικόνα, ωστόσο, οι αστυνομικές αρχές περιγράφουν μια οργανωμένη δραστηριότητα με εικονικές εταιρείες, αδιαφανή διαχείριση εκατομμυρίων ευρώ, στοιχηματισμό και φερόμενη χειραγώγηση ποδοσφαιρικών αγώνων. Η έρευνα επιχειρεί πλέον να αποτυπώσει το πλήρες οικονομικό δίκτυο και τον ρόλο κάθε εμπλεκόμενου προσώπου. Ρεπορτάζ: Σοφία Ορφανού, Γιώργος Γεραφέντης, Νίκος Κουντούρης, Δέσποινα Κρητικού, Τίμος Φακαλής, Κώστας Μπούρης, Σπύρος Δαρσινός, Κατερίνα Φάκα www.ertnews.gr

items.titleOriginal: When a 100-Year-Old Peepal Was Cut Down, He Used a 50-Tonne Crane to Replant It. Now It’s Growing
items.description: Τον Νοέμβριο του 2022, όταν ο Bharat Sisodia και η ομάδα του έφτασαν σε μια τοποθεσία στο Ahmedabad, βρήκαν ένα αιωνόβιο δέντρο peepal που είχε ήδη κοπεί. Μόνο περίπου έξι έως επτά πόδια από τον κορμό του απέμειναν. Για ένα δέντρο που στεκόταν εκεί για σχεδόν 100 χρόνια, φαινόταν σαν το τέλος. Αλλά ο Bharat ήθελε να μάθει αν οι ρίζες του ήταν ακόμα ζωντανές. Εάν en…
items.descriptionOriginal: In November 2022, when Bharat Sisodia and his team reached a site in Ahmedabad, they found a century-old peepal tree that had already been cut down. Only about six to seven feet of its trunk remained. For a tree that had stood there for nearly 100 years, it seemed like the end. But Bharat wanted to find out whether its roots were still alive. If enough of the root system had survived, perhaps the tree could grow again. What followed was an ambitious rescue. His team dug around the tree, brought in a 50-tonne crane and carefully moved what remained of it nearly two kilometres to another location. There, they replanted it in a specially prepared pit and continued caring for it as it recovered. The peepal has since reportedly begun showing new growth. The soil that travels with the tree's roots also plays a role in transplantation, helping the root system retain some of its original growing environment. Photograph: (Videograb-Catch Foundation) For Bharat, this was a reminder of something he has believed for years: planting a tree is only the beginning of the responsibility we have towards it. Since 2014, he has been working on an idea he calls 'plantenance', a combination of planting and maintenance. It focuses on giving trees the care they need to survive and grow, whether they have just been planted or have been standing for decades. At a time when roads, buildings and other infrastructure are reshaping our cities, his work raises an important question. When an old tree stands in the way of development, can we find a way to save it? Speaking to The Better India , Bharat shares what went into rescuing the peepal, why moving a mature tree requires such careful planning, and what cities can do to protect the trees they already have. Could a century-old tree survive after being cut down? When Bharat and his team arrived at the site, their first concern was the tree's roots. A tree that has been cut back so severely cannot simply be lifted out of the ground and replanted with the expectation that it will survive. Its chances of recovery depend on how much of its living root system remains intact and whether it can cope with the disturbance of being moved. The team began by digging a trench approximately six feet deep around the peepal. They then used water to soften the surrounding soil, making it easier to carefully free the roots. Moving a tree of this size required heavy machinery, manpower and careful preparation. A 50-tonne crane was brought in to lift the tree, which was then transported nearly two kilometres to its new location. View this post on Instagram A post shared by The Better India (@thebetterindia) At the new site, the team had prepared a planting pit with soil treatments and nutrients to support the tree's recovery. Once it was replanted, they continued looking after it. That care was especially important because the move had placed the tree in unfamiliar ground. Its roots would have to recover and establish themselves again so they could draw enough water and nutrients from the soil to support new growth. Several factors could influence its recovery, including the tree's condition before transplantation, the extent of damage to its roots and the weather in the weeks that followed. For Bharat, getting the peepal safely into the ground was an important first step. The next challenge was helping it stay alive. Why Bharat believes planting a tree is only the first step Every year, tree-planting drives bring thousands of new saplings into our cities and neighbourhoods. But how many of those saplings are still alive a few months later? A newly planted sapling needs regular watering, suitable soil, the right seasonal conditions and continued attention. Without that care, even a promising plantation drive can struggle to produce healthy, mature trees. Bharat believes the same responsibility applies when an existing tree is moved. He calls this approach 'plantenance', bringing planting and maintenance together so the focus remains on a tree's long-term survival. "An important part of plantenance is understanding what a tree needs after it has been planted or transplanted," he explains. Unlike moving an ordinary object from one location to another, transplanting a tree means disturbing a living root system that has spent years growing into its surroundings. The recovery process can take weeks or months, depending on the tree's condition and the weather. According to Bharat, favourable monsoon conditions can help a transplanted tree recover. Its roots may need at least two months to begin rebuilding, although the actual time depends on how much of the original root system remains intact and the damage it has sustained. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Bharat Sisodia (@bharatsisodiaofficial) Protecting the main root system is especially important. If those roots are badly damaged during excavation or transportation, the tree may struggle to absorb the water and nutrients it needs. This is why his team assesses the condition of each tree before deciding how to dig around it, lift it and transport it. And because every tree is different, the same method cannot be applied to every rescue. How far can an old tree be moved safely? Finding a suitable new home for a mature tree requires just as much thought as moving it there. When Bharat and his team plan a transplantation, they generally look for a site within the same region, preferably close to where the tree originally stood. Depending on the circumstances, they may move a tree around 10 kilometres. In some cases, the distance can extend to 15 to 20 kilometres. The aim is to find a location where the tree has a reasonable chance of adapting and growing again. Keeping the move relatively local can help because the environmental conditions are likely to be more familiar. The soil that travels with the tree's roots also plays a role in transplantation, helping the root system retain some of its original growing environment . "Understanding the environment is essential," Bharat says. The month, weather and temperature all need to be considered, along with the tree's condition and the suitability of its new location. A crane may make it possible to move a mature tree, but its future depends on what happens before and after the move. The Ahmedabad peepal is one example of how Bharat's team approaches a damaged tree. Another incident, involving a fallen banyan tree on Ahmedabad Airport Road, shows why he believes protecting trees must begin with the conditions in which they grow. When concrete leaves a banyan tree struggling to grow Banyan trees are known for their spreading branches and extensive root systems. As they mature, aerial roots grow down from their branches towards the ground. Over time, some of these roots develop into additional supporting trunks, helping the tree spread and support its growing canopy. But in cities, the space around a tree is often covered with concrete or other hard surfaces . Bharat recalls a banyan tree that had fallen on Ahmedabad Airport Road. When his team examined the site, they found that the cemented surroundings had restricted the development of its aerial roots. The tree had been growing in an environment where the roots that could have helped support its weight had limited room to develop. According to Bharat, his team eventually removed the fallen tree from the site, and he describes the operation as successful. The incident highlighted a problem that extends well beyond one banyan tree. For a mature tree, the space beneath and around the ground matters as much as the branches and leaves we see above it. Photograph: (Catch Foundation) "Compacted soil, sealed surfaces and inadequate space can affect root development. When the conditions that support a tree's growth are compromised, its long-term stability and health may also be affected," he shares. For a mature tree, the space beneath and around the ground matters as much as the branches and leaves we see above it. And once a tree becomes unstable or falls, rescuing it can require a much larger effort . In Vasai, saving trees became a community effort Bharat's work has also taken him beyond Ahmedabad. In Vasai, Maharashtra, he says his team helped relocate nearly 50 trees that were facing removal in connection with work by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). The effort required machinery and manpower, along with the involvement of people living in the area. Local residents and leaders participated in the work, and the team hired people from the community to help with the transplantation. For Bharat, their involvement made an important difference. "Community involvement is really important," he says. "When we have to transport trees, we need people to help. Local residents can make a real difference." View this post on Instagram A post shared by Bharat Sisodia (@bharatsisodiaofficial) Moving a mature tree involves digging around its roots, carefully lifting it, arranging transportation, preparing the new site and ensuring that it receives the care it needs afterwards. Having local people participate makes it possible for the community to contribute directly to protecting the trees around them. It also reflects the thinking behind Bharat's idea of plantenance: keeping trees alive is an ongoing responsibility that people can share. Can a newly planted sapling replace a 100-year-old tree? A mature tree has spent decades growing its roots and canopy. In that time, it has become part of its surroundings, providing shade, supporting birds and other wildlife, and contributing to the biodiversity of the area. Planting a new sapling is valuable, but that young tree will need years to grow and begin providing many of the same benefits. Bharat also recognises that moving an old tree comes with its own limitations. "Their ecological functions cannot be replicated immediately by planting a young sapling in their place. Equally, transplanting a mature tree does not automatically preserve all the ecological benefits it provided at its original location," he adds. The rescue of the Ahmedabad peepal offers an example of what may still be possible after a tree has suffered severe damage. But Bharat does not believe that every felled tree can necessarily be saved. Much depends on its condition, the health of its roots and the care it receives during and after transplantation. For India's growing cities, the larger challenge lies in preventing mature trees from reaching that point. Planning roads and buildings around existing trees, leaving enough room for roots to grow, providing suitable planting conditions and ensuring long-term maintenance can all help protect the greenery already present in our neighbourhoods. The century-old peepal in Ahmedabad was given another chance after it had been cut down. Its rescue leaves us with a question worth asking whenever an old tree stands in the path of development: could we give it the space and care it needs to keep growing right where it is?

Το νέο υλικό συνδυάζει κηροζίνη, λ…
items.descriptionOriginal: Concordia University researchers developed a kerosene-based gel that addresses a longstanding challenge in space propulsion: keeping fuel stable in storage and letting it flow into engines. A kerosene-based gel developed by Concordia researchers could make rocket and satellite fuels easier to store and control. The new material combines kerosene, lecithin, and calcium chloride to produce a gel that behaves more like a soft solid at rest but flows when subjected to force or heat, according to a study. Liquid fuels can slosh around tanks, complicating spacecraft control. A press release by Concordia continues that conventional gel fuels, however, can be difficult to work with. The new gel is designed to solve this problem. The research, conducted by Pranay Mudaliar and Jerin John, an associate professor of mechanical, industrial and aerospace engineering at Concordia University, examines how the gel responds to shear, temperature, and the addition of ethanol. Their findings, published in Langmuir , could help address the challenges the industry faces with conventional liquid and gel propellants, including fuel movement inside tanks and pumping fuel into engines. Its transparent appearance could also help researchers observe how fuel moves and burns. The problem of fuel Liquid propellants, because of their material, can become unstable. But fuel gels present other challenges, as they are difficult to pump and spray. So Concordia researchers developed this novel material that can act as both. When at rest, it remains solid, but when exposed to force or heat, it flows. The study explains that calcium chloride turns lecithin into long, worm-like structures called micelles. These structures form a mesh-like network that immobilizes the kerosene, producing a material with liquid and solid-like properties. The gel exhibits strong shear thinning, meaning its viscosity decreases 100 times as the shear rate increases, which is the secret sauce to making rocket and satellite fuel easier to store and deliver to engines. At rest, the gel, as a solid, could reduce problems caused by liquid fuel , such as movement and leakage, according to the university. Now, as a gel, the researchers had to figure out how to transform it into a liquid. According to the study, they used heat. At 138°F to 154°F, depending on the gel’s density, it transitioned into a liquid state, potentially offering a way to control fuel flow during propulsion operations . But adding ethanol caused the gel to liquefy almost immediately because it disrupts the micellar network that keeps the material in gel form. How long can it remain in storage? Researchers wanted to know if the material could maintain its structure in storage. According to Concordia University , samples remained stable for more than a year in sealed containers. The study reported that oscillatory testing saw an elastic linear viscoelastic regime below 1% strain. This’s associated with the gel’s ability to be stored long term. They also studied stress and strain on the material, which might cause the gel’s structure to break down. In short, this study showed how the material responds to mechanical force, temperature, and chemical changes, but its effectiveness in real propulsion systems remains to be established. Further testing is needed.

items.descriptionOriginal: In an Oct. 28 letter from the editors , Life Magazine — which was founded in 1936 and became an icon of visual storytelling — announced it will begin publishing again after nearly 20 years. Its first new print issue “offers a window into an America searching for meaning.” That 250-page edition hits newsstands Nov. 23, The New York Times reported , the inaugural step forward in a revival made possible by Bedford Media’s acquisition of the publication in 2024. The holding company was founded the year prior by model Karlie Kloss and is co-owned by her husband, venture capitalist Joshua Kushner. More than 120 people put together the forthcoming issue, focusing on “finding the ordinary in the extraordinary, and the extraordinary in the ordinary,” per the editors’ letter. The reincarnated brand will expand into other avenues as well, amplifying its quarterly print pieces through digital storytelling, documentaries, and events. © CORBIS—Corbis/Getty Images When Henry Luce founded Life , at the tail end of the Great Depression and three years before World War II began, the intent was to “harness the emerging power of photojournalism,” the letter reads. Luce had co-created Time magazine 13 years prior to deliver a concise weekly news digest to busy readers. Life took an opposite approach, inviting Americans to pore over dramatic multi-page photo spreads and essays that told stories about 20th-century topics large and small: from groundbreaking science and civil rights to movie stars and the lives of everyday people. The first issue came out Nov. 23, 1936 ( you can scroll through it in its entirety online ). The cover story captured one of the major public works projects in development under then-President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s historic New Deal, and Page 2 featured a photo of a baby held upside down by a doctor moments after birth. RELATED: Gordon Parks: How Life Magazine’s First Black Staff Photographer Shed Light on Social Justice With Expressive Images That view into the miracle of life (no pun intended) likely felt unprecedented to readers at the time. The newborn was George Story, who went on to become a journalist and liked to joke at parties that a nude picture of him had once been published in a national magazine. Santi Visalli/Getty Images After nearly four decades, Time Inc. ceased weekly publication of Life in 1972, citing production costs. The magazine returned in 1978 as a monthly publication and ran until 2000. In a full-circle moment, its final issue in that format also featured Story — this time covering his death at age 63. It was resurrected again in 2004 as a weekly newspaper supplement, but shut down three years later due to a decline in newspaper readership and ad sales, the company said, per NBC News. The upcoming revival marks exactly 90 years since Life began. Take a look back at some of its most iconic photos and covers. Τα σχόλια ξεκίνησαν σχεδόν αμέσως. «Εντάξει, λοιπόν, παρατήρησα ότι ξύνεις τον πατέρα…
items.descriptionOriginal: Abbie Herbert was 37 weeks into her third pregnancy in December 2025 when she decided to film a daily vlog until the baby arrived . In one of the first installments, posted to her TikTok account @abbieherbert , she absently scratched the palms of her hands on camera. The comments started almost immediately. “Okay, so I noticed you scratching the palms of your hands a lot in that video,” one viewer wrote . “If you’re having excessive itchiness on your hands and feet in pregnancy please ask your doctor to draw your bile acids to test for intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy.” Herbert, a 29-year-old content creator in Pittsburgh with over 15 million followers, figured it was probably just a flare-up of her eczema. Having already been through two pregnancies, she didn’t think much of it. “I was like, I know everything. This is nothing new,” she told TODAY . She looked up ‘cholestasis’ anyway and decided her symptoms didn’t match. The medical descriptions all centered on relentless, maddening itching, and hers felt minor. Still, both her mother and ChatGPT advised her to get checked just in case. A few days later, following a home photo shoot, she looked down at her palms and noticed a rash across both of them. It wasn’t especially itchy, she said, but it looked like tiny broken blood vessels covering her hands. Remembering the warnings from her comment section, she took a photo and sent it to her doctor, though she later admitted she hesitated because she worried about bothering the office over what looked like a few dots on her skin. Her doctor’s office called back immediately and told her to come in for blood work. Her bile acid levels came back at roughly double the normal threshold. By 6 a.m. the next day, her doctor called with instructions to head straight to the hospital. Herbert had planned to spend that day shopping for baby supplies. Instead, she underwent an urgent C-section, and her son, Rocky Blue, was born safely about two days after the first comments appeared on her video. Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy is a liver condition that typically develops in the third trimester, when normal bile flow slows down and bile acids build up in the bloodstream. Left untreated, elevated bile acids raise the risk of preterm birth, breathing problems for the baby, and stillbirth. Levels can change within a day, which is why doctors move fast once the numbers come back high. Herbert’s case was unusual in the exact way that nearly caused her to ignore it since the textbook presentation is intense itching on the palms and soles, particularly at night, with no visible rash. She had a visible rash and very little itching, so almost like the opposite of what most medical guides were describing. When she talked the experience in a post in October, she repeated the advice that caught her case which is if your hands or feet itch late in pregnancy, ask your doctor for a bile acid blood draw. Her comment section has since filled up with other mothers who caught the condition the same way. “Because of you, I told my doctor and was induced + c-section at 38 weeks pregnant,” one wrote. “Never heard of it before that; my baby is now 7 months old.” The post She scratched her hands in a pregnancy vlog. Strangers in the comments told her to call her doctor immediately. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: During the Golden Age of Hollywood , stars were often discovered in everyday settings, whether hanging out in a café, working at a drug store, or waiting tables in the Valley. One of the era’s most legendary stories is that the actress Lana Turner was discovered as a teenager at a Hollywood soda fountain. These days, it’s rare for someone to become famous just because they’re good-looking and in the right place at the right time. Actors get jobs only after navigating a gauntlet of casting directors, agents, auditions, and social media. The dream of hopping on a bus, getting off in LA, and being famous in six months has long gone. Chris Pratt and Zoe Saldana speaking at the 2016 San Diego Comic Con International, for “Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2”, at the San Diego Convention Center in San Diego, California. Photo credit: Gage Skidmore/Wikimedia Commons An exception to the current rule is Guardians of the Galaxy and Jurassic World star Chris Pratt . Actor-director Rae Dawn Chong cast him in his first film after he waited on her at a restaurant. Only this time it wasn’t at a chic place on Sunset Blvd., but a Bubba Gump Shrimp Company in Hawaii. Rae Dawn Chong is the daughter of comedian Tommy Chong, who is best known for starring in Quest for Fire (1981), The Color Purple (1985), and Commando (1985). After studying acting at a local community college for half a semester, a buddy invited him to come out to Hawaii, where he lived in a van. ”I had a friend who was like, ‘Dude, you’ve got to come out here,”’ Pratt told Entertainment Weekly . ”We set up camp on the beach and lived the dream. Pratt recently shared the story in an X post. Before Hollywood, I was living in a van in Hawaii and waiting tables at Bubba Gump Shrimp Company. One day, the incredible Rae Dawn Chong walked into the restaurant, and naturally, I went up to her table and said, “Hey, you’re a movie star! What are you doing here?” She asked if… pic.twitter.com/GCjsZpT5oY — Chris Pratt (@prattprattpratt) October 29, 2026 One day, the incredible Rae Dawn Chong walked into the restaurant, and naturally, I went up to her table and said, “Hey, you’re a movie star! What are you doing here?” She asked if I could act, and I said, “F**k yeah, put me in your movie!” She asked for my phone number. The only problem was I didn’t have one. So I gave her my buddy Mike’s number instead. A couple days later, Mike casually mentions, “Oh, by the way, someone called you.” ARE YOU KIDDING ME, MIKE?! I called her back, and sure enough, she was serious. I drove over to pick up the script, went back to Mike’s house, and read all 120 pages three times in a row. First script I’d ever read. My character’s name was Devon, and I remember thinking, “Sweet! I could totally play a Devon!” I showed up to the audition with every line and inflection mapped out in pencil. Rae told me I could act and offered me the part. I asked if we were shooting in Hawaii. Nope. Los Angeles. I had about $60 to my name, a bag of clothes, and some rollerblades. Then Rae told me they’d fly me out. And I remember thinking right then and there, my life just changed forever. I’m going to be an actor. They filmed Cursed 3 , a low-budget horror-comedy that was never released, but it launched Pratt’s career as an actor. After filming Cursed 3 , Pratt had a few minor roles and was cast as a high school jock in Everwood (2002–06). He later appeared in Parks and Recreation (2009–15) and in films including Moneyball (2011) and Zero Dark Thirty (2012). He later earned leading-man status after being cast in Guardians of the Galaxy (2014) and Jurassic World (2015). Of course, Pratt was asked to audition because he was charming and good-looking, two qualities essential to being a film star. However, none of it would have happened if he hadn’t been open to new experiences and willing to take risks to pursue his dreams. His story isn’t just about being in the right place at the right time; it’s about having the faith in yourself to take the opportunity, no matter how far-fetched it seems. The post Chris Pratt writes unbelievable post about how he got his first Hollywood job while waiting tables in Hawaii appeared first on Upworthy .

It hasn’t been formally scheduled yet or anything but she’s been trying to… — Womansplainer (@iWomansplainer) October 25, 2026 A staggering six million viewers saw the post, and many chimed in with strong opinions on both sides. What’s fascinating is how the debate and discourse evolved far beyond this mom’s specific situation. Some offered simple advice to that end: “An invitation isn’t a summons. If you’re not excited about the prospect of going, politely decline,” one commenter aptly suggested. But the conversation quickly broadened and tackled the very nature of adult friendships, especially between parents and their child-free friends. One side says: kid-free events are too big an ask of parents On the one hand, asking a parent of a very young child to leave them for several days when they can’t get home quickly, or to arrange familial or extremely expensive round-the-clock childcare, is a monumental ask. Many commenters expressed their frustration at weddings, social gatherings, and vacations that aren’t welcoming to children. “The ‘no kids’ culture is so weird to me. It’s not like she’s turning 21. She’s 30! I guess I’m at an age where I don’t want any extended outing to be off-limits to my kids, and no trip is as enjoyable without them as it is with them.” “Does she have kids? Like do people not get when you have kids that’s who you want to be with lol idk I would never do it unless kids were invited” These folks have a point. If it feels like kids are becoming welcome in fewer and fewer spaces, that’s because it’s true. Child-free weddings are on the rise. Parents are openly shamed on social media when their kids aren’t properly “trained” for restaurants or airplane behavior . It can be frustrating and cause families to simply isolate themselves and save everyone the hassle. Others disagree: parents must prioritize friendships Another strong cohort weighed in with an alternative take: imagine being the friend and realizing someone you’re close with is “mortified” by your birthday plans. Take it a step further: maybe being too anxious to be away from your toddler isn’t so good. “If she just didn’t want to go to your bachelorette party, bridal shower or baby shower you’d be upset. Don’t go if you don’t want to but then don’t act like this friendship is important to you now. This is why childfree people have a hard time maintaining friendships with parents” “Be honest with your friends, but also don’t be opposed to leaving your toddler overnight. It’s often good to get a break from your children and believe me I know I [raised] four kids!” “What happened in the last generation that has made parents so anxiously attached to their kids that they forfeit their own lives and friendships to avoid getting a babysitter?” “not being able to separate from your toddler for more than a day seems excessive” Others felt frustrated on behalf of the friend in this scenario. “as a single childless woman, you can show up for countless bridal showers, weddings, baby showers, kid’s birthday parties, anniversary dinners etc. but if you want even a modicum of reciprocation suddenly it’s mortifying and beyond the pale.” “I would hate to be y’all’s friends, simply not going and planning a dinner with them earlier would have sufficed, Tweeting about how you passively aggressively think I’m doing too much for my birthday … is nuts” The truth of this fascinating, thoughtful discourse likely lies somewhere in the middle. Parents and child-free people can be great friends, but these moments often carry natural tension and conflict. Any adult friendship, but especially between people in different life phases or with different lifestyles, requires effort from both parties. It requires the child-free friends to get to know the kids, be part of their lives, and show up for the family. But yes, it also requires parents to make the time and effort to keep the friendship going. Sometimes it might even mean leaving the kids at home. Child-free people need their friends to show up for them, too. What doesn’t work is letting our community, our village, and our social networks collapse. Journalist, author, and culture critic Anne Helen Peterson writes of this very dynamic: “Friendship means sometimes doing things that are tedious, or gross, or not what you’d like to spend your Sunday afternoon doing, because we all, at some point, need help with things that are tedious, and gross, and that we ourselves would rather not spend a Sunday afternoon doing. There are also very fun ways that we care for each other. But it’s a real weave. The good and the bad, the joyful and the slog, the visible and invisible — these are the ways we care for each other.” The post A mom was invited on a no-kids couples getaway, igniting a massive debate about adult friendships appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: Former First Lady Rosalynn Carter was married to President Jimmy Carter , who served as the 39th President of the United States from 1977 to 1981. The couple grew up together in Plains, Georgia. “She’s the girl I want to marry,” Jimmy Carter , three years her senior , reportedly told his mother after their first date, when Rosalynn was 17. The two married on July 7, 1946, and were together for 77 years before she passed away at 96 on November 19, 2023. President Carter would follow a little over a year later on December 29, 2024. In life, the Carters loved to cook, and Rosalynn’s Southern roots shone through her dishes. In fact, her cooking was so good that the U.S. National Archives recognized one standout: her “Plains Special” Cheese Ring. Rosalynn Carter’s cooking Jimmy once told The Washington Post , “We divide the responsibility. I’m a fairly good cook. I like Southern foods, corn on the cob, collard greens and turnips, grits, fried chicken. I like plain food.” Rosalynn also said , “When we were first married, Jimmy cooked as much as I did.” Growing up on a farm, Rosalynn Carter preferred fresh ingredients and was concerned about food additives early on. She reportedly tried to “read ingredients” on food packages, saying, “You have to know what you’re eating!” When back home in Georgia, one of the first things she would do was “to go to the store and buy fresh vegetables because we got so few vegetables when we were traveling.” Here's another #RosalynnCarter favorite – the "Plains Special" Cheese Ring! (strawberries optional this time). https://t.co/JH508WYzKm pic.twitter.com/KUl3Am45wn — U.S. National Archives (@USNatArchives) November 21, 2023 Eating in The White House Things changed once the Carters moved into the White House. They now had an entire staff, which included four chefs, to prepare meals for them. In an interview, Jimmy Carter told Oprah Winfrey that though they were no longer cooking for themselves, they still ate Southern classics: “The favorite meal is country food. When we got ready to move into the White House, Rosalynn went in—one of our staff members did—and asked the cooks and so forth at the White House, ‘Do you think you can make the kind of meals that the Carters are going to enjoy?'” President Carter said. He continued, “And their response was, ‘Yeah, we’ve been cooking that kind of meal for the servants for the last 20 years.'” Rosalynn Carter’s cheese ring recipe Now for Rosalynn’s nationally recognized cheese ring. If you’re so inclined, you can whip up the former First Lady’s recipe in minutes for your next holiday gathering or party. Here’s how to do it, with a few helpful tips from Southern Living : To prevent the mixture from sticking to the ring mold, Southern Living recommends lining it with plastic wrap before adding the good stuff. While it’s best served with crackers, you can also serve it with fresh veggie slices or toasted pita. Ingredients 1 lb. grated sharp cheese 1 cup finely chopped nuts 1 cup mayonnaise 1 small onion, finely grated Black pepper Dash cayenne Strawberry preserves (optional) Directions Combine all ingredients except preserves; season to taste with pepper. Mix well and place in a 5- or 6-cup ring mold. Refrigerate until firm, for several hours or overnight. To serve, unmold and, if desired, fill the center with strawberry preserves, or serve plain with crackers. The post First Lady Rosalynn Carter’s cheese ring is an easy, historic appetizer to serve this holiday season appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: “The Naming of Cats is a difficult matter, it isn’t just one of your holiday games…” – T.S. Eliot One of the best parts of getting a new pet is choosing a name for them. Unlike children, who have conscious feelings about their names and may object to off-the-wall choices at some point, a pet presumably couldn’t care less what the humans in their lives call them. A dog could be named Fred, Red, or Potatohead and be none the wiser. We’ve seen cats with names that go far beyond the norm even for pet names, like Parking Lot, Crunchwrap Supreme, and Missile Launcher (Missy for short) among other creative monikers. But if any animals were going to care about what we name them, surely it would be our finicky feline friends . And one man, whom we’ll call Unc (for his @UncGotThaMunchies handle), seems to have a gift for giving kitties very special (or rather, “pecial”) names. As of late 2025, Unc was the father of 13 kitties, and his naming of cats had become a bit of a viral phenomenon. Meet Unc’s growing kitty family First, there’s Blackaroni and Cheese, a black and orange kitten pair that people are just gaga over. But Unc has begun a whole movement of naming kitties in a “berry pecial” way, with Hersberry leading the way. Why Hersberry? Because her’s berry pecial to Unc, of course. Among the other kittens, we have another pair named Thor and Lowkey (yes, spelled Lowkey) and another orange kitty that Unc named Midas, “because there Midas well be no other kitties on the whole planet.” Now strangers want his help too People have become so enamored with these cute and clever kitty names that some have started asking Unc to help them name their own kittens. One person shared a photo of their adorable orange kitten and asked if Unc could name him because they couldn’t think of a good name. Unc didn’t disappoint. “When people see dis kitty right here,” he said in a response video. “They will say, ‘Oh, dis kitty is so beautiful. Oh, dis kitty is so pecial.’ So I think his name should be O’dis.” Then he explained all the nickname benefits of the name O’dis and how special this name would make the kitty feel. Someone else shared a photo of their fuzzy little tabby kitten, writing, “First I saw your Hersberry video then Midas and now the universe sent us a kitten and we can’t think of a name for her. Can you help name her??” Unc responded with a video saying that he’d had a premonition as he was laying around looking at kitties on TikTok that a beautiful little girl kitty was going to come to him needing a name, and he should have the name ready for her when he saw her. Watch how that played out: Did he choose a perfect name or what? The kitten’s owner responded in the comments and said, “Won’Da it is!! Thank you!!” Unc got a photo of another orange kitten with a name request. This one got the name Nuffin: “Because there is nuffin on dis Earf more cuter than this kitty. And there is nuffin on dis Earf that I would not do for this kitty. And there is nuffin on this whole Earf that could keep me from loving this kitty,” explained Unc. Of course. People are loving watching Unc name other people’s kitties, with multiple people calling him a walking green flag. “There is nuffin on this earf as precious as you naming kitties,” wrote one commenter. “There is nuffin I love more than a man who loves his kitties as much as you do!!” “Another perfect name!!! My sister is adopting a kitty today and I’ve been telling her about your names and how you come up with them. It’s great.” It’s not just the names people love Ultimately, the way Unc interacts with his kitties is what keeps people coming back. There’s something so endearing about the mutual affection between him and the whole lot of them. Not all cats are sweet and snuggly, but Unc’s kitties seem to be quite affectionate. People with more standoffish cats may be wondering why this man’s cats and kittens are so loving. Well, here you go: So berry, berry pecial. You can follow Unc on TikTok . This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. The post Man’s unique gift for naming cats has strangers asking him to name their kittens appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: Parents and grandparents find themselves at odds frequently. It could be a disagreement over how much screen time the kids get, battles over grandma giving them too many sweets, or arguments around how often grandma and grandpa should be babysitting . Conflict in their relationships is almost a given, and navigating disagreements in a healthy, productive way is key for the relationship to evolve and grow. One huge source of that conflict comes in the form of… stuff! All parents can relate to the sense of dread they feel at the sight of the grandparents arriving for a visit with a trunk full of presents. Toys, furniture, costumes, decor, you name it. And that’s just on a regular Tuesday. Around the holidays, it can get even worse. It’s not that they don’t want their kids getting gifts, it’s just all too much, especially when you live in a home with a finite amount of storage. Meet the grandma behind the idea DeeDee Moore , a grandma behind the website More Than Grand, shared on her TikTok account in November 2024 that “too much stuff” given from grandparents to their grandkids is one of the main sources of holiday frustration for parents. “75% of the parents that we surveyed wished grandparents would respect their wishes about gifts,” she explained (the figure comes from More Than Grand’s own survey), noting that while there are myriad reasons why this would be the case, the most common one (and incidentally the one most “waved off” by the grandparents) is the lack of physical space to accommodate. Now, you might be thinking: How much harm can it really do to give a kid a new card game or a baby doll? Certainly those don’t take up that much room. But when Moore breaks down the math, it’s a bit hard to deny. “Say your grandson has four other grandparents and four aunts and uncles. Each of these people get him one gift for a second birthday. That’s already nine gifts plus something for mom and dad. We’re up to 10,” she said. “If all of those grandparents buy him three things, and two of the aunts get him a little extra something, that’s 22 presents for a 2 year old who would be just as happy with a box.” Add in gifts from friends, and random gift-dumps from grandma when she’s been on a hot streak at the thrift store, and you’ve got a serious storage problem on your hands. @morethangrand Gifts should be a joy for both the giver and recipient, but at this time of year, they can end up being a source of conflict. Watch for a tip on how to channel your grandparent generosity! For more ways to navigate hotspots during upcoming holidays, make sure you are on our email list! Go to my bio to sign up! #grandparents #grandparent #CommunicationTips #GrandparentsLove #AdultChildren #NewGrandparent #newgrandma #newgrandparents #newgrandma #Grandparenting #grannytok #HealthyBoundaries #Boomer #EffectiveCommunication #GentleGrandparenting ♬ original sound – MoreThanGrand The math really adds up fast Yikes, gotta admit that’s a lot. And that’s not counting the additional problems too much gift-giving can incite listed on the More Than Grand website, which included: Undermining the parent’s values that they are trying to instill in their children Damaging a child’s ability to use their imagination Normalizing overconsumption Teaching children to associate seeing grandma or grandpa with getting a gift, rather than focusing on the actual relationship Here’s a bonus: Too many gifts steal Mom and Dad’s thunder! Parents often put a lot of thought into picking out presents they know their kids will love, only for them to get buried in the avalanche of surprise presents. These are all good points, and yet, what to do with all those good intentions and a desire to spoil some precious little nugget? Luckily, Moore has the perfect fix. “While your grandchildren are faced with getting too many gifts, many children are in the opposite situation. Take some of the things you bought to Toys for Tots or another organization that provides gifts for less fortunate families.” This allows folks to step into the “true spirit of giving,” Moore concluded. (Note that Toys for Tots accepts only new, unwrapped toys, so used or thrifted items are better donated to a thrift store, shelter, or daycare.) People had their own gift ideas too Viewers by and large seemed to agree, though many also noted how powerful experiential or future-building gifts could be, even if they’re not as cute as toys or as fun to open. @morethangrand How often do we hear “it takes a village to raise a child’? Grandparents can be that village, but it can be hard to show up the way today’s parents need. We created a digital grandparenting course that will teach you everything you need to know to be the village for your grandchild’s parents. It’s called New Grandparent Essentials, and you can find a link in my profile! It’s the best investment you can make in your family as you become a grandparent! #grandparents #grandparent #CommunicationTips #GrandparentsLove #AdultChildren #NewGrandparent #newgrandparents #newgrandma #Grandparenting #grannytok #HealthyBoundaries #Boomer #EffectiveCommunication #GentleGrandparenting ♬ original sound – MoreThanGrand “My in-laws opened up a college fund for both my kids. Instead of stuff they put more money in the account. I’m so grateful!” one person wrote. Another added, “I am giving experiences and putting money in an account for future needs (college, 1st house, starting business, etc).” A couple more tips to keep in mind In that vein, here are two other tips grandparents can use for intentional gift-giving… Open up a discussion with the parents. See if they need help with a big ticket item, find out which hobby or sport the child is interested in, ask what’s a definite “no.” This can save a lot of headaches for everyone. “The gifts should surprise the grandkids, not their parents,” as one commenter wrote on the video. 2. Prioritize memories over stuff. A trip to the zoo, an education membership, a ticket for two to the movies… these are often the gifts that truly keep on giving. And grandparents, don’t forget: just because you’re honoring boundaries, it doesn’t mean you have to pass up that sweet little something you see in the aisles. After all, shopping is fun, and it’s even better when you find a great deal or a cool discovery. But it can easily go to a little one who could really use it. For even more tips on all things grandparenting, follow More Than Grand on TikTok . This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. The post Grandma offers wake-up call for grandparents who can’t stop buying the grandkids presents appeared first on Upworthy .

items.description: Όλα τα παλιά είναι καινούργια και το ίδιο ισχύει και για τις κλασικές συνταγές. Για όσους μεγάλωσαν τη δεκαετία του 1970 (δηλαδή Baby Boomers και Generation Jones), τα βασικά πιάτα που σερβίρονταν στο τραπέζι του δείπνου ανακαλύπτονται ξανά στο Reddit από νεότερες γενιές που αναζητούν χορταστικά, ανακουφιστικά και οικονομικά γεύματα. Σύμφωνα με το JSTOR Daily, ηθοποιός…
items.descriptionOriginal: All things old are new again, and the same goes for classic recipes . For those who grew up during the 1970s (that’s Baby Boomers and Generation Jones ), staple dishes that were served at the dinner table are being rediscovered on Reddit by newer generations looking for filling, comforting, and affordable meals . According to JSTOR Daily , actress Liza Minnelli was perhaps the first to coin the modern usage of “comfort food” back in 1970. Minnelli told syndicated food columnist Johna Blinn , “Comfort food is anything you just yum, yum, yum.” Meals from the 1970s are nostalgic and also budget friendly. Try making one of these comforting recipes from Redditors that will fill you up and not break the bank. These are home cooks’ memories rather than tested recipes, so use a food thermometer and follow the USDA’s safe minimum internal temperatures : 160°F for ground meat and egg dishes like quiche, 165°F for poultry and casseroles, and 145°F plus a three-minute rest for pork chops. Can anybody please share any recipes for dinner from the 1970s? by u/WeirdoFromHighSchool in Old_Recipes 14 dishes worth remembering Tuna casserole “I LITERALLY made a tuna casserole last night & had the leftovers for lunch today.” – Disastrous-Soup-5413, RogerClyneIsAGod2 Turkey (or chicken) tetrazzini “ Tetrazzini is a creamy pasta dish with turkey (or chicken), mushrooms, and cheese.” – Disastrous-Soup-5413 Liver and onions “ Liver and onions , mashed potatoes and a green salad made with iceberg lettuce, tomatoes cut in wedges, cucumber slices… peeled, and Miracle Whip salad dressing.” – Kaktusblute Quiche Lorraine “A family favorite quiche recipe from the 1970’s. The secret? Half a cup of mayonnaise and an unreasonable quantity of cheese. My mom uses sweet onion instead of green onion, but otherwise made as written: 1/2 c. real mayonnaise 1/2 c. milk 2 eggs 1 Tbsp. corn starch 1 1/2 c. cubed cooked ham 1 1/2 c. (about 1/2 pound) chopped Swiss cheese 1/3 c. sliced green onion Dash pepper 1 unbaked 9″ pastry shell Mix together real mayonnaise, milk, eggs and corn starch until smooth. Stir in ham, cheese, onion and pepper. Turn into pastry shell. Bake in 350 degree Fahrenheit oven 35-40 minutes until golden brown on top and knife inserted comes out clean.” – banoctopus Cheese fondue “For fondue, you can go in a few different directions. Cubed crusty bread is one of the classic ways to dip into cheese fondue , but you could use fruits, vegetables, chunks of cooked or cured sausages, so long as they will keep their structural integrity.” – Bluecat72 Meatloaf and baked potatoes “A basic meatloaf is ground beef, minced onions, bread crumbs, an egg and a squirt of ketchup for moisture, salt, pepper, garlic powder.. whatever you like. Get your hands in there and squish it all together until thoroughly mixed. Form into a vague loaf shape on a pan and bake at 350 for an hour. Poke a couple potatoes with a fork and cook them in the microwave for 5-7 minutes. Enjoy a meatloaf sandwich with mustard for lunch the next day.” – yblame Pork chops with rice and cream of mushroom soup “Brown the chops, take them out of the pan, pour in rice, soup and water, stir to combine. Put the pork chops on top. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes or until rice is cooked. Tossed green salad: iceberg lettuce, chopped scallions, tomatoes, cucumbers, Wishbone Italian Dressing.” – hicjacket Salmon croquettes “ Salmon croquettes were a staple of my childhood. Canned salmon, saltine crackers, and an egg. We called them croquettes but naw, they were shaped into salmon patties.” – DazzlingBullfrog9, throwawaytodaycat Mexican casserole “Brown ground beef, stir in a can of tomato sauce and 1 sliced green onion. Mix together a cup of sour cream, a cup of cottage cheese and a can of chopped green chilies. In a 9×13 pan, layer crushed tortilla chips, meat, cream mixture and grated Colby-jack or Colby cheese. Repeat layers. Bake until hot and bubbly.” – Open-Gazelle1767 Hamburger Stroganoff “One pound ground beef, 1 package Lipton onion soup mix, 1 can cream of mushroom or chicken soup, sour cream. Brown the ground beef, stir in the can of soup and soup mix. Stir in the sour cream until it looks right…I think it’s a half pint, but maybe a whole pint. Serve over rice for the 2 kids who eat rice and egg noodles for the one kid who doesn’t.” – Open-Gazelle1767 Shake ‘N Bake Chicken “ Shake’n Bake chicken or pork chops. ‘And I helped!’ Preheat oven to 400F. Moisten chicken with water. Place breasts in Shake-n-Bake shaker bag. Shake the bag vigorously to coat the chicken. Bake for 20 minutes if boneless, 45 minutes if it does have bones.” – Karin58 Grilled cheese and tomato soup “Still my favorite thing to eat, but now I make my own tomato bisque, my own bread, and use Gouda or cheddar. Back then Mom made this for Friday lunch: Campbell’s tomato soup (made with milk) and the grilled cheese was two slices of five-loaves-for-a-dollar white bread with Velveeta, grilled with Miami Maid margarine in the Revere Ware skillet.” – Mindless_Pop_632, mulberryred Pork sausage and rice “I grew up in the 70s and my mother made this sausage and rice dish at least once a month. The recipe is from Peg Bracken’s I Hate To Cook Book . Crumble 1 to 1 1/2 pounds of pork sausage (hamburger will do, but pork is better) into a skillet and brown it. Pour off the fat. Add: 1 green pepper, chopped 2 green onions, chopped 2 or 3 celery stalks, chopped 2 c. chicken consommé or bouillon 1 c. raw rice 1 tbsp. Worcestershire sauce 1/2 tsp. salt Put on the lid and let it simmer at lowest possible heat for 1 hour.” – officerbirb Sloppy Joes “ Classic Sloppy Joes . My family had these regularly in the ‘70s.” – ThatPtarmiganAgain Dishes worth bringing back There’s a reason these recipes keep resurfacing on Reddit decades after they first showed up on dinner tables. They’re cheap, they’re filling, and they taste like someone’s kitchen, not a restaurant trying to impress you. You don’t need fancy ingredients or a complicated technique to make a meal that people remember. items.descriptionOriginal: When people think of portraits from the Victorian era , the images that come to mind are usually women in tight corsets with extremely pale skin . Children were also very pale and often appeared to have dark circles under their eyes. But why? It’s not because they had better sunscreen in the 1800s. The reason many people who posed for those portraits looked as white as bleached cotton sheets is multifaceted. Painted portraits from the Victorian era generally depicted wealthy people, which likely explains the over-the-top dresses and hairstyles. Photographs are a different story: by the 1860s, the carte de visite and cheaper processes like the tintype made portraits affordable to far more people . And early photographic emulsions were very sensitive to blue light, so yellows and reds came out too dark , which can make skin look washed out and eyes shadowed. Because these images are in black and white, they can’t tell us what people’s complexions actually looked like. Why pale skin meant power back then In the 1800s , especially during the Victorian era, paleness indicated status. The paler you were, the more money you were assumed to have, signaling higher social status. It was believed that tan skin meant you did some form of outdoor manual labor, something associated with poorer people. Paintings from that era often show women enjoying the outdoors in multilayered dresses, carrying parasols to shield their fair skin from the sun. This belief that paleness displayed high status became a dangerous obsession, according to historians. Then tuberculosis became fashionable The Johnston Collection explains that the Romantic period marked a shift toward paleness and extreme thinness as the ultimate signs of wealth and beauty, writing, “many of the beauty icons of the day were depicted as skeletal thin with ghostly pale skin, glistening eyes, flushed cheeks and perpetually red lips.” Those chasing this impossible beauty standard quickly noticed that contracting tuberculosis produced many of these highly sought-after features as the disease progressed. “If a lady wasn’t fortunate enough to suffer from such a glamorous illness, she could feign going into a decline, the desirable fragile look being simulated by drinking vinegar and dropping belladonna into the eyes,” The Johnston Collection notes. Belladonna is poisonous, but women of the era appeared unafraid to risk death for the privilege of being seen as beautiful. As the Romantic period faded, appearing sickly did not fall out of fashion. The Victorian era simply tied paleness to morality and social status, leading women to continue risking their lives to avoid being perceived as poor. Instead of trying to contract tuberculosis, women began ingesting arsenic, chalk, and even ground-up rocks to maintain a fair complexion. History Facts shares: “In 1851, a Swiss physician published a report in a medical journal about the ‘toxicophagi,’ a group of people in modern-day Austria who routinely consumed arsenic; they knew it was poison, but thought they could develop an immunity to it by starting with small doses and gradually increasing the intake. The report’s author claimed that arsenic gave them great energy, sparkling eyes, and wonderful complexions, but noted that after long-term use, unsurprisingly, ‘most arsenic eaters end with an inevitable infirmity of the body.'” And then the wallpaper started killing people While there was some knowledge that consuming arsenic could be dangerous, it was still viewed as benign when used in other products. The chemical was used to create the color green in clothing, wallpaper, and other products. This led children to take on the same sickly look and eventually contributed to their deaths. Unintentionally, entire families were poisoned by their beautiful green wallpaper, dresses, baby blankets, and other household items. With: Arsenic greens turned up in wallpaper, dresses, hats, and even children’s toys, and children were among the victims. Unintentionally, families were poisoned by their beautiful green wallpaper, dresses, and other household items. Dampness made things worse: mold growing on the wallpaper could release a toxic arsenic gas, as Italian chemist Bartolomeo Gosio showed in the 1890s. In one 1862 case in east London, children died in a home after doctors first blamed their illnesses on diphtheria. Accounts say physician Dr. Thomas Orton later tested the green wallpaper in the children’s playroom and found it contained arsenic. Cases like it helped turn Victorian tastes away from the deadly dyes. If you ever find yourself gazing up at a portrait of a ghostly pale Victorian child or a wealthy Victorian woman, remember that arsenic was one of the dangers of the age, even if status, fashion, and early camera chemistry explain much of the pallor. Ingesting deadly chemicals to keep up appearances is a practice that should probably stay lost to history. And Victorian arsenic still turns up today: the Poison Book Project has now identified 515 arsenic-laced emerald-green bookbindings in libraries around the world. This article originally appeared in January. It has been updated. The post Historians explain why everyone was so darn pale in those Victorian-era portraits appeared first on Upworthy .

Οι κβαντικοί υπολογιστές θα μπορούσαν τελικά να βοηθήσουν σε ορισμένα από αυτά τα προβλήματα, ενδεχομένως να ανοίξουν…
items.descriptionOriginal: Imagine designing a better battery, discovering a new medicine, or developing a material that can withstand extreme temperatures. Even the world’s most powerful supercomputers can struggle to simulate the behavior of complex molecules and materials accurately. Quantum computers could eventually help with some of these problems, potentially opening doors to discoveries that are difficult or prohibitively expensive today. But don’t expect a quantum computer to replace your laptop or suddenly solve every problem that conventional computers cannot. Its potential is much more specialized. And while companies are racing to build increasingly powerful machines, the most important applications are still taking shape. So, what could quantum computers actually solve, and how long might we have to wait? First, what makes quantum computers different? Traditional computers process information using bits, which represent either a 0 or a 1. Quantum computers use quantum bits, or qubits, which can exploit phenomena such as superposition and entanglement to perform certain calculations in fundamentally different ways. This does not mean they try every possible answer simultaneously. As the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) explains in its quantum computing guide , extracting useful information from a quantum calculation requires carefully designed algorithms. Their advantage comes from the ability to manipulate complex quantum states, making certain problems potentially much easier to tackle than with conventional computing. The catch? Qubits are extremely fragile. Small disturbances can introduce errors, and researchers need increasingly sophisticated error-correction systems before quantum computers can reliably perform lengthy calculations. 1. Designing better medicines and chemicals One of the most promising applications is quantum chemistry. Molecules behave according to quantum mechanics, which makes quantum computers a potentially natural tool for simulating them. Even powerful classical computers struggle to accurately model certain complex chemical interactions, particularly in systems involving strongly correlated electrons. Quantum computers could eventually simulate these interactions more directly, helping researchers understand how molecules behave and react. That could have implications for drug discovery, chemical manufacturing, and the development of more efficient catalysts. For example, researchers could investigate molecular structures and reaction pathways to identify promising compounds or chemical processes. A particularly interesting possibility is developing better catalysts for producing ammonia, a key ingredient in fertilizer manufacturing . More efficient chemical reactions could also help reduce the energy required for industrial production. A 2025 research perspective published in the Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation , involving researchers from several national laboratories and universities, identified potential applications in photochemistry and materials design using early fault-tolerant systems with approximately 25 to 100 logical qubits. When? Early, scientifically meaningful demonstrations could emerge as fault-tolerant systems become available over the next few years. Broader applications in pharmaceutical development and industrial chemistry will likely take longer, potentially extending into the 2030s. 2. Discovering better batteries and materials What if researchers could simulate a material’s properties before spending years developing and testing it in a laboratory? Quantum computers could help investigate the behavior of electrons in complex materials, potentially improving the search for better battery components, superconductors, solar cells, and industrial materials. This is closely related to the chemistry problem, but the implications extend into energy and manufacturing. Better simulations could help researchers understand why certain materials conduct electricity, store energy, or exhibit unusual magnetic properties. The US Department of Energy’s Quantum Genesis initiative specifically identifies chemistry, materials science, plasma physics, and high-energy physics as potential application areas. Research applications could begin gaining traction in the late 2020s, with more substantial materials-discovery applications potentially emerging during the 2030s. These are estimates, not guaranteed delivery dates. 3. Breaking today’s encryption Not every potential quantum application is something to look forward to. Many widely used encryption systems rely on mathematical problems that are extremely difficult for conventional computers to solve. One example is the factorization of very large numbers, which underpins the security of RSA encryption. In 1994, mathematician Peter Shor developed a quantum algorithm that could theoretically solve this problem efficiently. A sufficiently powerful quantum computer running this algorithm could threaten RSA and other public-key cryptographic systems. That does not mean today’s quantum computers can crack bank accounts or unlock encrypted internet traffic. They are nowhere near the required capabilities. However, the threat is serious enough that governments and technology companies are already preparing alternatives. NIST has published post-quantum cryptography standards designed to withstand attacks from both conventional and future quantum computers. The US Government Accountability Office reported in October 2026 that experts believe a cryptographically relevant quantum computer could emerge as soon as the 2030s, although estimates vary. The threat is a 2030s concern, not an established capability today. The transition to quantum-resistant encryption is already underway because sensitive information collected now could remain valuable for decades. 4. Tackling complicated optimization problems Quantum computers could also help with problems involving enormous numbers of possible combinations. Consider organizing airline schedules, optimizing industrial supply chains, managing electricity grids, or coordinating complex manufacturing operations. Finding the best solution among countless possibilities can become computationally expensive. Quantum algorithms may eventually help explore certain optimization problems more efficiently, particularly when combined with conventional computers. However, this is one area where expectations need to be tempered. There is no established evidence that quantum computers will routinely outperform the best classical methods across everyday business optimization problems. When? Experimental applications are already being explored, but commercially meaningful advantages remain uncertain. Some optimization problems may benefit during the late 2020s or 2030s, while others may never offer a worthwhile quantum advantage. So, when does the quantum era actually begin? There is no single arrival date. IBM’s current quantum roadmap targets a large-scale fault-tolerant system for 2029, while the US Department of Energy’s Quantum Genesis initiative aims to demonstrate scientifically relevant fault-tolerant systems by 2028. These are ambitious development targets, not guarantees that commercially useful breakthroughs will follow immediately. The likely future is not quantum computers replacing conventional machines. Instead, they will work alongside classical supercomputers and AI systems, handling specialized calculations that are particularly difficult for traditional hardware. The first big breakthroughs may not come as a flashy new consumer gadget. Instead, they could show up as a better battery, a more efficient industrial chemical process, or a new understanding of how a complex molecule behaves.
